research.centralQuestion: How does McDonald's generate billions when selling cheap burgers?
research.businessMechanism: McDonald's operates primarily as a commercial real estate landlord; 39% of total company revenue ($10 billion) is pure rent paid by franchisees on land owned under restaurants.

verifiedFacts.claim: McDonald's 2024 rent revenue from franchisees was $10,017 million.
Over ninety five percent of McDonald's restaurants worldwide are franchised.

doNotClaim: Rent is the 10-K 'Rents' revenue line, not profit.
Do not say McDonald's owns every restaurant.

dialogue.speaker: host
dialogue.text: Our last video about McDonald's blew up, and the comments are fighting over Ray Kroc. But almost nobody knows where their money actually comes from.

dialogue.speaker: insider
dialogue.text: Because McDonald's isn't a burger chain. They're a ten billion dollar real estate landlord.

dialogue.speaker: insider
dialogue.text: The burgers are just the bait. Ray Kroc's genius was buying the physical land under every restaurant. If a franchisee wants to sell fries, they have to pay McDonald's rent first.

dialogue.speaker: host
dialogue.text: So they make more from rent than burgers?

dialogue.speaker: insider
dialogue.text: Thirty-nine percent of their entire revenue is pure rent. Over ninety-five percent of restaurants are franchised. McDonald's is a real estate monopoly in disguise.
